svg.title: Figure 5-10. Loss scenarios: the panda, the harness box and the car's controllers (C3 to C6) (WP-A-05 §5)
svg.desc: Figure 5-10: 9 loss scenario cards for the panda, the harness box and the car's controllers (C3 to C6). LS-04 (UCA-35, Known gap): The panda watchdog resets the MCU while engaged. The MCU boots SILENT with the siren off. Only the SoC alerts, within 0.5 s. Steering and braking stop at once; the panda's own siren cannot sound. Engaged flag across reset decided, not implemented; TSR-516 not amended; bench confirmation open. LS-05 (UCA-32, UCA-13, Covered): controlsd stalls while pandad keeps sending heartbeats. About 0.1 s of a repeated in-limit command (by design); the arrival check revokes at about 0.16 s, with the siren. Authority is kept briefly on stale data. Covered in the reference build (default since e84f850); not verified on the vehicle. LS-07 (UCA-33, Covered): The panda hangs with the intercept switches driven. A watchdog reset after about 90 ms releases the switches; a forwarding stall with the MCU running is not caught. Stock PCS frames are not forwarded while the switches intercept. Covered for a hang (bench confirmation open); known gap for forwarding stalls. LS-08 (UCA-42, Open test): The item blocks the stock camera's LKA/ACC messages. The camera receives no feedback for them. It sets a fault that also disables PCS; only a vehicle test can tell. Open test: needs a vehicle test (OI-5). LS-11 (UCA-30, Known gap): The envelope limits are the controller limits. Torque 1500, rate 15/25, deceleration −3.5 m/s² on both sides: no margin, nothing derived from the vehicle. Requests outside the controllable envelope pass. Envelope needs vehicle measurements that do not exist yet. LS-21 (UCA-31, Known gap): The brake frame 0x226 has no checksum or counter. A stuck 'not pressed' value with live timing passes. The panda keeps authority while the driver brakes. GAP-01: 0x226 has no checksum or counter; diverse PCM path needs a vehicle test. LS-22 (UCA-34, Known gap): The intercept switches stay in pass-through while the item transmits. Stock and item frames both reach the car; no switch position is fed back. Stock LKA/ACC messages are not blocked. Readback needs the hardware change DQ-209 decides. LS-32 (UCA-36, Known gap): The ignition branch to the harness box opens, or its supply shorts. The switches' state is undefined, and nothing in the item sees the stock path. The item stays engageable while stock PCS is lost. Waits on DQ-209 and the bench results. LS-33 (UCA-33, Known gap): Pull-down R2 or R3 is open (latent). Nothing shows it until the panda stops driving the switches; then they may stay in intercept. Stock PCS frames are neither passed through nor forwarded. Latent fault with no monitor until readback exists.

How each unsafe control action comes about: the cause, what the controller believes or never learns, and the action on the road.
Steps: 1 the cause · 2 named after the scenario's causal-factor type · 3 the unsafe control action

watchdog reset) without the SoC announcing it

a failed release) while not forwarding stock PCS messages

UCA-42: Stops issuing PCS when it no longer sees its own LKA/ACC feedback
